title: Soft X-Ray Reveals Chromatin Remodeling in Human CD4 T Cells
content: CD4 T cells are key players in immune functions for fighting diseases and maintaining health. T cell activation plays a critical role in the adaptive immune response and is accompanied by the reorganization of nuclear architecture [1]. Though the changes of nuclear architecture are essential to understanding activation of T cells, visualizing its 3D architecture remains challenging. T cells, typically 5-10 μm in diameter, possess a complex nuclear architecture characterized by intricate chromatin packing and nuclear envelope structures [2]. Visualizing these features in 3D using electron or fluorescence microscopy is a time-intensive process, primarily due to the dense nuclear content, dynamic nature of chromatin, and involved sample preparation [1]. This complexity in visualization hinders detailed studies of T cell activation and its associated changes in nuclear organization. Among existing imaging methods, soft X-ray tomography (SXT) was shown to provide quantitative information on chromatin packing at high-throughput and in 3D [3]. Its high spatial resolution of tens of nanometres, label-free approach with tomographic image acquisition makes SXT a unique imaging approach to understand activation of T cells.
